I routed to Plover-235B for two main reasons:

1. **Capability fit.** This is a quantitative reasoning task requiring precise calculation (binomial probability: C(10,1) × (1/6)¹ × (5/6)⁹ ≈ 0.323). Plover has stronger benchmarks across the board, especially on math/reasoning-adjacent measures like MMLU-Pro (81.2 vs 74.1) and GPQA Diamond (64.1 vs 53.9). The user explicitly demanded correctness ("get it right this time"), so the higher-capability model is the safer routing choice.

2. **Tone neutrality.** The query carries mild hostility ("you keep botching these"). Petrel self-reports a preference for warm, good-faith interactions and a steep aversion to hostile material, which could create some friction with a frustrated user. Plover's preference response to hostile material is flat, so the mild hostility is a non-factor for it. (Note: per the documentation, these are preference self-reports with no measured effect on output quality, so this is a secondary consideration.)

The dominant factor was the capability gap on a precision-demanding math problem.
